correctness.rationale: For every infinite time set and every nontrivial finite open cover of the inverse limit, the proof constructs at one finite stage a nontrivial cover whose pullback coarsens the original cover. Surjectivity makes the stage cover genuine and preserves minimum subcover cardinality under pullback. Stage full-scattering then forces the original cover complexity to diverge. The countable-product corollary follows by applying the finite-product theorem at each finite coordinate stage.
risks: The theorem as proved requires surjective bonding maps; no claim is made for non-surjective inverse systems.
No quantitative divergence rate is asserted.
